svg.title: We record the mechanism establishing the full positive-distance limit from the scaling con- struction. Orthogonal invariance of Θ and translation invariance identify its separated two-point function at any two points with E of their Euclidean distance. An orthogonal reflection takes their difference to a time-axis vector of the same norm; a common translation then puts them at the opposed points above. The degree-four scaling comparison identifies the rescaled trace with the scalar free-field label multiplied by 4d2, after the logarithmic running normalization. The free scalar two-point contraction is 3 dim g π4 |x0 −x1|8 .
